content:
Naval just said what VCs have been whispering for 18 months.

Pure software is un-investable. Not dying — un-investable. The margin compression from AI is real and it's accelerating.

---

Here's the flip side nobody's saying out loud: this is the best thing that ever happened to crypto.

Protocol-layer value doesn't compress. Scarcity doesn't get vibe-coded away. The asset layer wins when the software layer commoditizes.

---

We spent a decade arguing crypto needed a "killer app." Turns out the killer thesis was simpler: own the layer AI can't replicate.

Where are you repositioning right now — software or protocol layer?
source_story_title: Naval Declares 'Pure Software Is Rapidly Becoming Un-Investable'
source_story_summary: Naval Ravikant posted a terse but high-signal observation that pure software companies are rapidly losing their investment appeal, garnering over 14,000 likes and 1,200 retweets — among the highest engagement of any post in the dataset. While no elaboration was given, the statement is widely interpreted in the context of AI commoditizing software development and compressing software margins.

content:
A decade. That's how long Ethereum has been trying to fix its own onboarding problem from the inside.

EIP-8141 isn't a feature drop. It's the protocol finally catching up to what builders have been duct-taping together with smart contract wallets for years.

---

The real signal: when the base layer stops being the bottleneck, product quality becomes the only moat.

No more blaming gas UX. No more apologizing for seed phrases. The excuses are gone.

---

Every wallet and consumer crypto app needs to be asking one question right now: what were we building around that we no longer have to?

The constraint just changed. Does your roadmap reflect that?
source_story_title: Vitalik Details EIP-8141: The Omnibus Account Abstraction Solution After a Decade of Effort
source_story_summary: Vitalik Buterin posted a deep-dive on EIP-8141, describing it as an omnibus EIP that resolves every remaining open problem in Ethereum account abstraction — a goal the community has pursued since EIP-86 in early 2016. The post represents a significant milestone in Ethereum's UX and smart-wallet evolution, suggesting the long-promised AA endgame may finally be within reach.
